It is an important tourist destination, being frequented for recreational activities such as swimming, boating and trout fishing during the summer; a distinctive building in the lake is the half-submerged church of Saint Nicholas. Since 1952 it is part of the Mavrovo National Park. With its surface of 13.7 km2 (3,400 acres), is one of the most extensive artificial lakes of the country. 
The lake is surrounded by the Šar Mountains on the North and the Bistra Mountains on the South,  both exceeding heights of 2500 m.
